statement: Sections, torsors, and local conditions — Let $k$ be a number field, $X/k$ a smooth geometrically connected curve, and $b$ a rational point or rational tangential point. For a characteristic quotient $U$ of the geometric fundamental group, the section at $b$ identifies the corresponding arithmetic extension with $U\rtimes G_k$. Continuous splittings modulo conjugation by $U$ are the pointed set $H^1_{\rm cts}(G_k,U)$. For a unipotent $\Q_p$-group $U$, a Selmer scheme is a specified subset of this pointed set, cut out by ramification and local conditions. It is not the unrestricted set of splittings.

statement: All standard tripod dimensions through class eight — Put $X=\mathbb P^1_\Q\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$ and use the unit tangent at $0$. Let $S$ be a finite set of rational primes, $s=|S|$, and choose $p\ge5$ outside $S$. For $U_n=\pi_1^{\rm un}(X_{\overline\Q},b)/\gamma_{n+1}$ over $\Q_p$, impose unramifiedness outside $S\cup\{p\}$ and crystallinity at $p$. Write $\operatorname{Sel}_{S,n}$ for this standard Selmer scheme, without additional refined conditions at $S$. statement: The first dimension drops and integral finiteness — For each of $U_n$ and $M_n$, the first strict inequality \[ \dim\operatorname{Sel}_{S,n}<\dim H_f^1(\Q_p,U_n) \] (with $M_n$ substituted in its case) occurs at class $1,2,4$ for $s=0,1,2$, respectively. Each inequality implies that $X(\Z[1/S])$ is finite. It does not identify that set with the corresponding Selmer locus.

statement: Abelian approximations do not separate every cusp — For the tripod the unrestricted abelian section sets are \[ H^1(G_\Q,\widehat\Z(1)^2) =\left(\varprojlim_m\Q^\times/(\Q^\times)^m\right)^2, \qquad H^1(G_\Q,\Q_p(1)^2) =\left(\widehat{\Q^\times}^{\,p}\otimes_{\Z_p}\Q_p\right)^2. \] They are infinite. The two tangential sections at $0$ and $1$, using respectively parameters $z$ and $1-z$ with unit tangent, have the same class in both sets. Thus the assertion that distinct cusps remain nonconjugate in every abelian approximation is false. This counterexample concerns an approximation, and does not identify the full profinite cuspidal sections.

statement: The effect of the degree-seven nonpentagonal element — Let $\ell\ge5$ and let $\beta$ be the pro-$\ell$ element of B.12 with normalized conjugator $f$ having leading Lie term $q_7$. On $U_n$ it is the identity for $n\le7$. In class eight, with the normalization $\beta(x)=x,\ \beta(y)=f^{-1}yf$, its first change is \[ \beta(\log x)=\log x,\qquad \beta(\log y)=\log y+[\log y,q_7]\pmod{\text{degree}>8}. \] It transports cocycles for $\rho$ bijectively to cocycles for $\rho^\beta=\beta\rho\beta^{-1}$. It need not act on the section set for the \emph{fixed} action $\rho$. All tripod finiteness thresholds in F.3 occur before this change can be detected.

statement: The obstruction at each successive central extension — Let $1\to A\to U\to V\to1$ be a central extension of topological $G_k$-groups, with $A$ abelian and with continuous local lifts for the cocycles under consideration. For a $V$-cocycle $c$, choose a continuous lift $\widetilde c$. Its defect \[ o_c(\sigma,\tau)= \widetilde c_\sigma\,\sigma(\widetilde c_\tau) \widetilde c_{\sigma\tau}^{-1}\in A \] defines a class in $H^2_{\rm cts}(G_k,A)$ independent of the lift. The class vanishes exactly when $c$ lifts. For a fixed representative $c$, its lifts modulo $A$-conjugacy form a torsor under $H^1_{\rm cts}(G_k,A)$. Passing to $U$-conjugacy further divides by the stabilizer of $c$ in $V$. Local conditions impose the corresponding local obstruction and localization conditions.

statement: The condition for restricting a section to a cover — Suppose $1\to N\to P\to H\to1$ is an exact geometric finite-cover sequence, stable under the arithmetic action after a specified finite extension of the base field. If the chosen approximation preserves this exact sequence, a section of its arithmetic extension restricts to the cover exactly when its induced section of $H\rtimes G_k$ is the section specifying that cover, up to the stated $H$-conjugacy. Restriction after an open subgroup of $G_k$ is possible whenever the corresponding finite cocycle becomes trivial there.

statement: What the normalizer version does and does not supply — Replacing the arithmetic image by a Teichm\"uller normalizer does not by itself define a Selmer problem. Suppose an action on $U$ extends from an algebraic arithmetic image $A$ to a proalgebraic normalizer $N$. Then restriction defines \[ H^1_{\rm alg}(N,U)\longrightarrow H^1_{\rm alg}(A,U). \] For a faithfully flat image map $G\to A$ through which the action factors, inflation is injective and its image consists precisely of cocycles trivial on $\ker(G\to A)$. Neither operation supplies unramifiedness or crystallinity at a place.

statement: Lemmas that can be passed to the point-section problem — The following conclusions apply to a proposed point-section comparison only with their hypotheses. A point or rational tangential point gives a compatible section at every characteristic quotient. It restricts to a chosen finite cover exactly under F.11. If a unipotent quotient with the actual arithmetic action satisfies the local hypotheses of F.3 or F.8 and a strict global--local dimension inequality, its integral-point locus is finite. These facts do not prove that every section is geometric, or that a finite-level Kummer map is injective on all point and cusp packets.
